sanskrit: athābravīd dvijaṃ rāmaḥ kathaṃ te bhrātaro vane kīdṛśaṃ tu tadā brahmaṃs tapaś cerur mahāvratāḥ
english: Then Rāma spoke to the twice-born sage: "How did your brothers practice austerities in the forest, O Brahman? What manner of great vows did they undertake there?"

sanskrit: agastyas tv abravīt tatra rāmaṃ prayata mānasaṃ tāṃs tān dharmavidhīṃs tatra bhrātaras te samāviśan
english: Then Agastya spoke to Rāma, whose mind was pure and attentive: "Those brothers of his engaged in various ordained rules of dharma there."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇas tadā yatto nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ tatāpa graiṣmike kāle pañcasv agniṣv avasthitaḥ
english: Kumbhakarṇa, then ever diligent and devoted to dharma, performed austerities in the summer season seated amid five fires.

sanskrit: varṣe meghodakaklinno vīrāsanam asevata nityaṃ ca śaiśire kāle jalamadhyapratiśrayaḥ
english: In the rainy season, drenched by cloud-waters, he practiced the hero's posture; and in the winter season he constantly dwelt submerged in water.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa tasyāticakramuḥ dharme prayatamānasya satpathe niṣṭhitasya ca
english: Thus ten thousand years passed for him as he strove in dharma, fixed upon the straight path.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā nityaṃ dharmaparaḥ śuciḥ pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi pādenaikena tasthivān
english: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, ever devoted to dharma and pure, stood on one foot for five thousand years.

sanskrit: samāpte niyame tasya nanṛtuś cāpsarogaṇāḥ papāta puṣpavarṣaṃ ca kṣubhitāś cāpi devatāḥ
english: When his vow was completed, the troops of apsarases danced, a rain of flowers fell, and the gods were stirred with joy.

sanskrit: pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi sūryaṃ caivānvavartata tasthau cordhvaśiro bāhuḥ svādhyāyadhṛtamānasaḥ
english: For five thousand years he followed the course of the sun, standing with arms raised and head uplifted, his mind sustained by recitation of the Vedas.

sanskrit: evaṃ vibhīṣaṇasyāpi gatāni niyatātmanaḥ daśavarṣasahasrāṇi svargasthasyeva nandane
english: Thus for Vibhīṣaṇa too, whose self was disciplined, ten thousand years passed as if he were in heaven's Nandana grove.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasraṃ tu nirāhāro daśānanaḥ pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śiraś cāgnau juhāva saḥ
english: For ten thousand years Daśānana (Rāvaṇa) went without food; and at the completion of each thousand years he offered one of his heads into the fire.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi nava tasyāticakramuḥ śirāṃsi nava cāpy asya praviṣṭāni hutāśanam
english: Thus nine thousand years passed for him, and nine of his heads had entered the fire.

sanskrit: atha varṣasahasre tu daśame daśamaṃ śiraḥ chettukāmaḥ sa dharmātmā prāptaś cātra pitāmahaḥ
english: Then, at the tenth thousand-year period, just as he was about to sever the tenth head, the Grandsire (Brahmā) arrived there.

sanskrit: pitāmahas tu suprītaḥ sārdhaṃ devair upasthitaḥ vatsa vatsa daśagrīva prīto 'smīty abhyabhāṣata
english: The Grandsire, greatly pleased and accompanied by the gods, addressed him: "O child, O child, Daśagrīva — I am pleased with you."

sanskrit: śīghraṃ varaya dharmajña varo yas te 'bhikāṅkṣitaḥ kiṃ te kāmaṃ karomy adya na vṛthā te pariśramaḥ
english: "Ask quickly, O knower of dharma, whatever boon you desire; what wish shall I fulfil for you today? Your toil has not been in vain."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd daśagrīvaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā praṇamya śirasā devaṃ harṣagadgadayā girā
english: Then Daśagrīva spoke, his inner self filled with delight, bowing his head to the god, his voice choking with joy:

sanskrit: bhagavan prāṇināṃ nityaṃ nānyatra maraṇād bhayam nāsti mṛtyusamaḥ śatrur amaratvam ato vṛṇe
english: "O blessed one, for living beings there is always no fear other than death; there is no enemy equal to death — therefore I choose immortality."

sanskrit: suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṃ daityadānavarakṣasām avadhyaḥ syāṃ prajādhyakṣa devatānāṃ ca śāśvatam
english: "May I be forever invincible by Suparṇas (Garuḍas), Nāgas, Yakṣas, Daityas, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, and the gods, O Lord of creatures."

sanskrit: na hi cintā mamānyeṣu prāṇiṣv amarapūjita tṛṇabhūtā hi me sarve prāṇino mānuṣādayaḥ
english: "I have no concern with other living beings, O you who are worshipped by the immortals — all creatures such as humans are as grass to me."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā uvāca vacanaṃ rāma saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Daśagrīva the Rākṣasa, O Rāma, the righteous Grandsire spoke together with the gods:

sanskrit: bhaviṣyaty evam evaitat tava rākṣasapuṃgava śṛṇu cāpi vaco bhūyaḥ prītasyeha śubhaṃ mama
english: "It shall be exactly so for you, O foremost of Rākṣasas; and hear further my auspicious and gracious words here."

sanskrit: hutāni yāni śīrṣāṇi pūrvam agnau tvayānagha punas tāni bhaviṣyanti tathaiva tava rākṣasa
english: "Those heads you previously offered into the fire, O sinless one, shall be restored to you just as before, O Rākṣasa."

sanskrit: evaṃ pitāmahoktasya daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ agnau hutāni śīrṣāṇi yāni tāny utthitāni vai
english: Thus, as the Grandsire spoke to Daśagrīva the Rākṣasa, those heads that had been offered into the fire rose up again.

sanskrit: evam uktvvā tu taṃ rāma daśagrīvaṃ prajāpatiḥ vibhīṣaṇam athovāca vākyaṃ lokapitāmahaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Daśagrīva, O Rāma, Prajāpati — the Grandsire of the worlds — then spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa:

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇa tvayā vatsa dharmasaṃhitabuddhinā parituṣṭo 'smi dharmajña varaṃ varaya suvrata
english: "Vibhīṣaṇa, O child, by you whose intellect is grounded in dharma, I am fully satisfied; ask a boon, O knower of dharma, O one of good vows."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā vacanaṃ prāha sāñjaliḥ vṛtaḥ sarvaguṇair nityaṃ candramā iva raśmibhiḥ
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, spoke with joined palms, endowed always with all virtues as the moon is with its rays:

sanskrit: bhagavan kṛtakṛtyo 'haṃ yan me lokaguruḥ svayam prīto yadi tvaṃ dātavyaṃ varaṃ me śṛṇu suvrata
english: "O blessed one, I am already fulfilled in that the teacher of the worlds is himself pleased with me; yet if a boon is to be given me, hear my wish, O one of good vows."

sanskrit: yā yā me jāyate buddhir yeṣu yeṣv āśrameṣu iha sā sā bhavatu dharmiṣṭhā taṃ taṃ dharmaṃ ca pālaye
english: "Whatever understanding arises in me in whatever circumstances here, may that understanding always be directed toward dharma, and may I uphold that dharma."

sanskrit: eṣa me paramodāra varaḥ paramako mataḥ na hi dharmābhiraktānāṃ loke kiṃ cana durlabham
english: "This is the highest and most noble boon I have in mind; for those devoted to dharma, nothing in the world is unattainable."

sanskrit: atha prajāpatiḥ prīto vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha dharmiṣṭhas tvaṃ yathā vatsa tathā caitad bhaviṣyati
english: Then Prajāpati, greatly pleased, said to Vibhīṣaṇa: "As you are most devoted to dharma, O child, so it shall be."

sanskrit: yasmād rākṣasayonau te jātasyāmitrakarṣaṇa nādharme jāyate buddhir amaratvaṃ dadāmi te
english: "Since, though born in a Rākṣasa womb, O crusher of enemies, your understanding does not turn toward unrighteousness — immortality I grant you."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇāya tu varaṃ prayacchantam ariṃdama prajāpatiṃ surāḥ sarve vākyaṃ prāñjalayo 'bruvan
english: But as Prajāpati was about to grant a boon to Kumbhakarṇa, O subduer of enemies, all the gods with joined palms spoke:

sanskrit: na tāvat kumbhakarṇāya pradātavyo varas tvayā jānīṣe hi yathā lokāṃs trāsayaty eṣa durmatiḥ
english: "A boon should not be granted to Kumbhakarṇa by you; for you know how this evil-minded one terrifies the worlds."

sanskrit: nandane 'psarasaḥ sapta mahendrānucarā daśa anena bhakṣitā brahman ṛṣayo mānuṣās tathā
english: "Seven apsarases in the Nandana grove, ten attendants of great Indra, O Brahman, and sages and humans — all have been devoured by him."

sanskrit: varavyājena moho 'smai dīyatām amitaprabha lokānāṃ svasti caiva syād bhaved asya ca saṃnatiḥ
english: "Under the guise of a boon, let delusion be granted to him, O one of immeasurable radiance; thus the worlds will prosper and he will be subdued."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ surair brahmācintayat padmasaṃbhavaḥ cintitā copatasthe 'sya pārśvaṃ devī sarasvatī
english: Thus spoken to by the gods, Brahmā — born from the lotus — reflected; and as he reflected, the goddess Sarasvatī drew near to his side.

sanskrit: prāñjaliḥ sā tu parśvasthā prāha vākyaṃ sarasvatī iyam asmy āgatā devakiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇy aham
english: Standing at his side with joined palms, Sarasvatī spoke: "Here I have come, O god — what service shall I render?"

sanskrit: prajāpatis tu tāṃ prāptāṃ prāha vākyaṃ sarasvatīm vāṇi tvaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhava yā devatepsitā
english: To Sarasvatī thus arrived, Prajāpati spoke: "O Vāṇī (speech personified), enter into the lord of Rākṣasas as that which the gods desire."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā praviṣṭā sā prajāpatir athābravīt kumbhakarṇa mahābāho varaṃ varaya yo mataḥ
english: Saying "So be it," she entered him; then Prajāpati said: "O Kumbhakarṇa, O mighty-armed one, ask the boon you have in mind."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇas tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā vacanam abravīt svaptuṃ varṣāṇy anekāni devadeva mamepsitam
english: Hearing those words, Kumbhakarṇa spoke: "To sleep for many years — O god of gods, this is what I desire."

sanskrit: evam astv iti taṃ coktvā saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ devī sarasvatī caiva muktvā taṃ prayayau divam
english: Saying "So be it," the Grandsire together with the gods — and the goddess Sarasvatī having released him — departed to heaven.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇas tu duṣṭātmā cintayām āsa duḥkhitaḥ kīrdṛśaṃ kiṃ nv idaṃ vākyaṃ mamādya vadanāc cyutam
english: But Kumbhakarṇa of evil soul reflected in distress: "What manner of words indeed have now fallen from my mouth?"

sanskrit: evaṃ labdhavarāḥ sarve bhrātaro dīptatejasaḥ śleṣmātakavanaṃ gatvā tatra te nyavasan sukham
english: Thus all the brothers, having obtained their boons and blazing with splendour, went to the Śleṣmātaka forest and dwelt there in comfort.

sanskrit: sumālī varalabdhāṃs tu jñātvā tān vai niśācarān udatiṣṭhad bhayaṃ tyaktvā sānugaḥ sa rasātalāt
english: Sumālī, learning that those night-rangers had obtained their boons, rose up from Rasātala (the netherworld) together with his followers, having cast off fear.

sanskrit: mārīcaś ca prahastaś ca virūpākṣo mahodaraḥ udatiṣṭhan susaṃrabdhāḥ sacivās tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Mārīca, Prahasta, Virūpākṣa, and Mahodara — the ministers of that Rākṣasa — rose up with great eagerness.

sanskrit: sumālī caiva taiḥ sarvair vṛto rākṣasapuṃgavaiḥ abhigamya daśagrīvaṃ pariṣvajyedam abravīt
english: Sumālī, surrounded by all those foremost Rākṣasas, approached Daśagrīva, embraced him, and spoke:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā te putrasaṃprāptaś cintito 'yaṃ manorathaḥ yas tvaṃ tribhuvaṇaśreṣṭhāl labdhavān varam īdṛśam
english: "By good fortune this long-cherished wish of mine for a son has been fulfilled, that you have obtained such a boon, surpassing the three worlds."

sanskrit: yatkṛte ca vayaṃ laṅkāṃ tyaktvā yātā rasātalam tad gataṃ no mahābāho mahad viṣṇukṛtaṃ bhayam
english: "For whose sake we abandoned Laṅkā and went to the netherworld — that great fear created by Viṣṇu which beset us has now passed, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: asakṛt tena bhagnā hi parityajya svam ālayam vidrutāḥ sahitāḥ sarve praviṣṭāḥ sma rasātalam
english: "Time and again shattered by him, we all fled together, abandoning our own abode, and entered the netherworld."

sanskrit: asmadīyā ca laṅkeyaṃ nagarī rākṣasoṣitā niveśitā tava bhrātrā dhanādhyakṣeṇa dhīmatā
english: "This city of Laṅkā, formerly inhabited by us Rākṣasas, has been settled by your wise brother, the lord of wealth (Kubera)."

sanskrit: yadi nāmātra śakyaṃ syāt sāmnā dānena vānagha tarasā vā mahābāho pratyānetuṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "If it were possible, O sinless one, to reclaim it — whether by conciliation, by gifts, or by force, O mighty-armed one — that would be well done."

sanskrit: tvaṃ ca laṅkeśvaras tāta bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ prabhuś caiva bhaviṣyasi mahābala
english: "You shall become lord of Laṅkā, my child — there is no doubt; and you shall indeed become the master of all of us, O greatly powerful one."

sanskrit: athābravīd daśagrīvo mātāmaham upasthitam vitteśo gurur asmākaṃ nārhasy evaṃ prabhāṣitum
english: Then Daśagrīva spoke to his grandfather who stood before him: "The lord of wealth (Kubera) is our elder — you should not speak thus."

sanskrit: uktavantaṃ tathā vākyaṃ daśagrīvaṃ niśācaraḥ prahastaḥ praśritaṃ vākyam idam āha sakāraṇam
english: To Daśagrīva who had spoken thus, the night-ranger Prahasta spoke this humble yet reasoned speech:

sanskrit: daśagrīva mahābāho nārhas tvaṃ vaktum īdṛśam saubhrātraṃ nāsti śūrāṇāṃ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "O Daśagrīva, O mighty-armed one, you should not speak like this; among heroes there is no brotherhood — hear these words of mine."

sanskrit: aditiś ca ditiś caiva bhaginyau sahite kila bhārye paramarūpiṇyau kaśyapasya prajāpateḥ
english: "Aditi and Diti were sisters, it is said, two supremely beautiful wives of Kaśyapa Prajāpati."

sanskrit: aditir janayām āsa devāṃs tribhuvaṇeśvarān ditis tv ajanayad daityān kaśyapasyātmasaṃbhavān
english: "Aditi gave birth to the gods, the lords of the three worlds; Diti, however, bore the Daityas born of Kaśyapa."

sanskrit: daityānāṃ kila dharmajña pureyaṃ savanārṇavā saparvatā mahī vīra te 'bhavan prabhaviṣṇavaḥ
english: "Of the Daityas, O knower of dharma, it is said this city, this earth with its ocean-shores and its mountains — all belonged to them, O hero; they were supremely powerful."

sanskrit: nihatya tāṃs tu samare viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā devānāṃ vaśam ānītaṃ trailokyam idam avyayam
english: "But having slain them in battle, Viṣṇu the supremely powerful brought this imperishable triple world under the dominion of the gods."

sanskrit: naitad eko bhavān eva kariṣyati viparyayam surair ācaritaṃ pūrvaṃ kuruṣvaitad vaco mama
english: "You alone are not the only one who will reverse this; what the gods themselves did previously — do that; follow these words of mine."

sanskrit: evam ukto daśagrīvaḥ prahastena durātmanā cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ vai bāḍham ity eva so 'bravīt
english: Thus addressed by Prahasta, the evil-souled one, Daśagrīva reflected for a moment and then said simply: "Very well."

sanskrit: sa tu tenaiva harṣeṇa tasminn ahani vīryavān vanaṃ gato daśagrīvaḥ saha taiḥ kṣaṇadācaraiḥ
english: With that same joy, on that very day, the valiant Daśagrīva set out for the forest together with those night-rangers.

sanskrit: trikūṭasthaḥ sa tu tadā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ preṣayām āsa dautyena prahastaṃ vākyakovidam
english: Stationed at Trikūṭa, the night-ranger Daśagrīva then dispatched Prahasta, skilled in speech, as his emissary.

sanskrit: prahasta śīghraṃ gatvā tvaṃ brūhi nairṛtapuṃgavam vacanān mama vitteśaṃ sāmapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: "Prahasta, go quickly and speak to that foremost of Nairṛtas (Rākṣasas), the lord of wealth, these conciliatory words on my behalf:"

sanskrit: iyaṃ laṅkā purī rājan rākṣasānāṃ mahātmanām tvayā niveśitā saumya naitad yuktaṃ tavānagha
english: "'This city of Laṅkā, O king, belonging to the great-souled Rākṣasas, has been occupied by you, O gentle one; this is not fitting for you, O sinless one.'"

sanskrit: tad bhavān yadi sāmnaitāṃ dadyād atulavikrama kṛtā bhaven mama prītir dharmaś caivānupālitaḥ
english: "'If you were to yield it through conciliation, O one of incomparable prowess, my gratification would be secured and dharma upheld.'"

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā gatvā prahasto vākyakovidaḥ daśagrīvavacaḥ sarvaṃ vitteśāya nyavedayat
english: Thus instructed, Prahasta, skilled in speech, went and reported all the words of Daśagrīva to the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: prahastād api saṃśrutya devo vaiśravaṇo vacaḥ pratyuvāca prahastaṃ taṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: The god Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), having heard these words from Prahasta, replied to that Prahasta — himself expert in speech:

sanskrit: brūhi gaccha daśagrīvaṃ purī rājyaṃ ca yan mama tavāpy etan mahābāho bhuṅkṣvaitad dhatakaṇṭakam
english: "Go, tell Daśagrīva: 'This city and this kingdom of mine — O mighty-armed one, it is yours as well; enjoy it; the enemy has been destroyed.'"

sanskrit: sarvaṃ kartāsmi bhadraṃ te rākṣaseśa vaco 'cirāt kiṃ tu tāvat pratīkṣasva pitur yāvan nivedaye
english: "'I shall do all that is good for you, O lord of Rākṣasas, without delay; but meanwhile, wait until I inform my father.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā dhanādhyakṣo jagāma pitur antikam abhivādya guruṃ prāha rāvaṇasya yadīpsitam
english: Having spoken thus, the lord of wealth went to his father's presence; bowing to that elder, he reported what Rāvaṇa desired.

sanskrit: eṣa tāta daśagrīvo dūtaṃ preṣitavān mama dīyatāṃ nagarī laṅkā pūrvaṃ rakṣogaṇoṣitā mayātra yad anuṣṭheyaṃ tan mamācakṣva suvrata
english: "O father, this Daśagrīva has dispatched a messenger to me: 'Let the city of Laṅkā, formerly inhabited by the host of Rākṣasas, be given over.' Tell me what I should do here, O one of good vows."

sanskrit: brahmarṣis tv evam ukto 'sau viśravā munipuṃgavaḥ uvāca dhanadaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇu putra vaco mama
english: The brahmarṣi Viśravā, that foremost of sages, thus addressed, spoke to the wealth-giver: "Listen, my son, to my words."

sanskrit: daśagrīvo mahābāhur uktavān mama saṃnidhau mayā nirbhartsitaś cāsīd bahudhoktaḥ sudurmatiḥ
english: "The mighty-armed Daśagrīva spoke in my presence; I repeatedly rebuked him, and that utterly evil-minded one was repeatedly spoken to by me."

sanskrit: sa krodhena mayā cokto dhvaṃsasveti punaḥ punaḥ śreyo'bhiyuktaṃ dharmyaṃ ca śṛṇu putra vaco mama
english: "In anger I repeatedly told him to be destroyed; now hear my words, O son, which are directed toward what is best and in accordance with dharma."

sanskrit: varapradānasaṃmūḍho mānyāmānyaṃ sudurmatiḥ na vetti mama śāpāc ca prakṛtiṃ dāruṇāṃ gataḥ
english: "Deluded by the granting of boons, that utterly evil-minded one does not know what is worthy of respect and what is not; and through my curse he has attained a dreadful nature."

sanskrit: tasmād gaccha mahābāho kailāsaṃ dharaṇīdharam niveśaya nivāsārthaṃ tyaja laṅkāṃ sahānugaḥ
english: "Therefore go, O mighty-armed one, to mount Kailāsa, the bearer of the earth; settle there as your abode, and abandon Laṅkā together with your retinue."

sanskrit: tatra mandākinī ramyā nadīnāṃ pravarā nadī kāñcanaiḥ sūryasaṃkāśaiḥ paṅkajaiḥ saṃvṛtodakā
english: "There is the lovely Mandākinī, the foremost of rivers, her waters covered with golden lotuses bright as the sun."

sanskrit: na hi kṣamaṃ tvayā tena vairaṃ dhanadarakṣasā jānīṣe hi yathānena labdhaḥ paramako varaḥ
english: "Indeed it is not fitting for you to make enmity with that Rākṣasa (Rāvaṇa) who has obtained wealth — for you know what supreme boon he has obtained."

sanskrit: evam ukto gṛhītvā tu tad vacaḥ pitṛgauravāt sadāra pauraḥ sāmātyaḥ savāhanadhano gataḥ
english: Thus counselled, and accepting that advice out of reverence for his father, Kubera departed with his wives, his citizens, his ministers, his mounts, and his treasury.

sanskrit: prahastas tu daśagrīvaṃ gatvā sarvaṃ nyavedayat śūnyā sā nagarī laṅkā triṃśadyojanam āyatā praviśya tāṃ sahāsmābhiḥ svadharmaṃ tatra pālaya
english: Prahasta, going to Daśagrīva, reported everything: "That city of Laṅkā, thirty yojanas in extent, is empty. Enter it with us and uphold your duty there."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ prahastena rāvaṇo rākṣasas tadā viveśa nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ sabhrātā sabalānugaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Prahasta, Rāvaṇa the Rākṣasa then entered the city of Laṅkā together with his brothers and his army of followers.

sanskrit: sa cābhiṣiktaḥ kṣaṇadācarais tadā niveśayām āsa purīṃ daśānanaḥ nikāmapūrṇā ca babhūva sā purī niśācarair nīlabalāhakopamaiḥ
english: Anointed by the night-rangers, Daśānana then peopled the city; and that city became filled to satisfaction with night-rangers resembling dark stormclouds.

sanskrit: dhaneśvaras tv atha pitṛvākyagauravān nyaveśayac chaśivimale girau purīm svalaṃkṛtair bhavanavarair vibhūṣitāṃ puraṃdarasyeva tadāmarāvatīm
english: The lord of wealth, out of reverence for his father's words, then settled a city on that mountain bright as the moon — adorned with beautiful, well-decorated mansions, like Amarāvatī of Purandara (Indra).

sanskrit: rākṣasendro 'bhiṣiktas tu bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahitas tadā tataḥ pradānaṃ rākṣasyā bhaginyāḥ samacintayat
english: The lord of Rākṣasas, having been anointed, then together with his brothers thought about arranging the marriage of his Rākṣasa sister.

sanskrit: dadau tāṃ kālakeyāya dānavendrāya rākṣasīm svasāṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ nāma vidyujjihvāya nāmataḥ
english: He gave that Rākṣasī, his sister Śūrpaṇakhā by name, to Kālakeya, a lord of Dānavas, who bore the name Vidyujjihva.

sanskrit: atha dattvā svasāraṃ sa mṛgayāṃ paryaṭan nṛpaḥ tatrāpaśyat tato rāma mayaṃ nāma diteḥ sutam
english: Then, having given his sister away, that king while roaming on a hunt saw there, O Rāma, one named Maya, a son of Diti.

sanskrit: kanyāsahāyaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ apṛcchat ko bhavan eko nirmanuṣya mṛge vane
english: Seeing him accompanied by a maiden, the night-ranger Daśagrīva asked: "Who are you, alone in this uninhabited forest wilderness?"

sanskrit: mayas tv athābravīd rāma pṛcchantaṃ taṃ niśācaram śrūyatāṃ sarvam ākhyāsye yathāvṛttam idaṃ mama
english: Then Maya, O Rāma, spoke to that night-ranger who had inquired: "Hear — I shall relate to you the full truth of my circumstances."

sanskrit: hemā nāmāpsarās tāta śrutapūrvā yadi tvayā daivatair mama sā dattā paulomīva śatakratoḥ
english: "An apsaras named Hemā — if you have heard of her, O friend — was given to me by the gods, even as Paulomī was given to Śatakratu (Indra)."

sanskrit: tasyāṃ saktamanās tāta pañcavarṣaśatāny aham sā ca daivata kāryeṇa gatā varṣaṃ caturdaśam
english: "With mind attached to her, O friend, I spent five hundred years with her; then she, on account of some divine business, departed for fourteen years."

sanskrit: tasyāḥ kṛte ca hemāyāḥ sarvaṃ hemapuraṃ mayā vajravaidūryacitraṃ ca māyayā nirmitaṃ tadā
english: "For her sake, for Hemā, I constructed an entire golden city, variegated with vajra and vaidūrya gems, by my māyā power."

sanskrit: tatrāham aratiṃ vindaṃs tayā hīnaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ tasmāt purād duhitaraṃ gṛhītvā vanam āgataḥ
english: "Finding no peace there, bereft of her, deeply sorrowful, I took my daughter and came from that city to the forest."

sanskrit: iyaṃ mamātmajā rājaṃs tasyāḥ kukṣiu vivardhitā bhartāram anayā sārdham asyāḥ prāpto 'smi mārgitum
english: "This is my daughter, O king, who grew in her womb; I have come seeking a husband to be with her."

sanskrit: kanyāpitṛtvaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi narāṇāṃ mānakāṅkṣiṇām kanyā hi dve kule nityaṃ saṃśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati
english: "For being the father of a daughter is sorrow for men who aspire to honour; a daughter constantly keeps two families in a state of anxious uncertainty."

sanskrit: dvau sutau tu mama tv asyāṃ bhāryāyāṃ saṃbabhūvatuḥ māyāvī prathamas tāta dundubhis tadanantaram
english: "By this wife of mine, however, two sons were born to me: Māyāvī was the first, O friend, and Dundubhi after him."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ tvām idānīṃ kathaṃ tāta jānīyāṃ ko bhavān iti
english: "All this has been truthfully told to you who asked; how should I now know you, O friend — who are you?"

sanskrit: evam ukto rākṣasendro vinītam idam abravīt ahaṃ paulastya tanayo daśagrīvaś ca nāmataḥ
english: Thus addressed, the lord of Rākṣasas spoke humbly: "I am a son of Paulastya (Pulastya's lineage), and Daśagrīva is my name."

sanskrit: brahmarṣes taṃ sutaṃ jñātvā mayo harṣam upāgataḥ dātuṃ duhitaraṃ tasya rocayām āsa tatra vai
english: Knowing him to be the son of a brahmarṣi, Maya was filled with joy and resolved there to give him his daughter.

sanskrit: prahasan prāha daityendro rākṣasendram idaṃ vacaḥ iyaṃ mamātmajā rājan hemayāpsarasā dhṛtā kanyā mandodarī nāma patnyarthaṃ pratigṛhyatām
english: Smiling, the lord of Daityas spoke these words to the lord of Rākṣasas: "This, O king, is my daughter, carried by the apsaras Hemā — the maiden Mandodarī by name; accept her as your wife."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva taṃ rāma daśagrīvo 'bhyabhāṣata prajvālya tatra caivāgnim akarot pāṇisaṃgraham
english: O Rāma, Daśagrīva said simply "Yes" to him, kindled a fire there, and performed the rite of taking her hand in marriage.

sanskrit: na hi tasya mayo rāma śāpābhijñas tapodhanāt viditvā tena sā dattā tasya paitāmahaṃ kulam
english: For Maya, O Rāma, knowing the curse of the one rich in austerities, gave her to him knowing his ancestral lineage.

sanskrit: amoghāṃ tasya śaktiṃ ca pradadau paramādbhutām pareṇa tapasā labdhāṃ jaghnivāṃl lakṣmaṇaṃ yayā
english: And he gave him his unfailing and supremely wondrous weapon — obtained through the highest austerities — with which Lakṣmaṇa was later struck down.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa kṛtadāro vai laṅkāyām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ gatvā tu nagaraṃ bhārye bhrātṛbhyāṃ samudāvahat
english: Thus having taken a wife, that lord and master went to the city of Laṅkā and arranged wives for his brothers as well.

sanskrit: vairocanasya dauhitrīṃ vajrajvāleti nāmataḥ tāṃ bhāryāṃ kumbhakarṇasya rāvaṇaḥ samudāvahat
english: Rāvaṇa arranged as wife for Kumbhakarṇa the granddaughter of Virocana, named Vajrajvālā.

sanskrit: gandharvarājasya sutāṃ śailūṣasya mahātmana saramā nāma dharmajño lebhe bhāryāṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, the knower of dharma, obtained as wife Saramā by name, daughter of Śailūṣa, the great-souled king of Gandharvas.

sanskrit: tīre tu sarasaḥ sā vai saṃjajñe mānasasya ca mānasaṃ ca saras tāta vavṛdhe jaladāgame
english: She was born on the shore of the Mānasa lake, and that Mānasa lake, O friend, swelled at the coming of the rains.

sanskrit: mātrā tu tasyāḥ kanyāyāḥ snehanākranditaṃ vacaḥ saro mā vardhatety uktaṃ tataḥ sā saramābhavat
english: Her mother spoke words choked with affection to that girl-child: "O lake, do not swell" — and from that she became Saramā.

sanskrit: evaṃ te kṛtadārā vai remire tatra rākṣasāḥ svāṃ svāṃ bhāryām upādāya gandharvā iva nandane
english: Thus those Rākṣasas, having taken wives, sported there delightfully, each with his own wife, like Gandharvas in the Nandana grove.

sanskrit: tato mandodarī putraṃ meghanādam asūyata sa eṣa indrajin nāma yuṣmābhir abhidhīyate
english: Then Mandodarī gave birth to a son, Meghanāda — he who is called Indrajit by you.

sanskrit: jātamātreṇa hi purā tena rākṣasasūnunā rudatā sumahān mukto nādo jaladharopamaḥ
english: For the very moment that Rākṣasa's son was born, he cried out and released a mighty roar resembling that of a thundercloud.

sanskrit: jaḍīkṛtāyāṃ laṅkāyāṃ tena nādena tasya vai pitā tasyākaron nāma meghanāda iti svayam
english: When Laṅkā was stupefied by that roar of his, his father himself gave him the name Meghanāda ("Thunder-Roar").

sanskrit: so 'vardhata tadā rāma rāvaṇāntaḥpure śubhe rakṣyamāṇo varastrībhiś channaḥ kāṣṭhair ivānalaḥ
english: He grew up then, O Rāma, in the auspicious inner apartments of Rāvaṇa, guarded by noble women, concealed like fire within wood.
